_meta.name: AlmiOET origins library — destination-NEUTRAL — v4
_meta.supersedes_for_origins: The origin halves of AlmiOET_corridor_proof_batch_v3.json (which baked the UK destination into origin facts).
_meta.purpose: Fix the spine so origins reuse across destinations WITHOUT name-swaps. Each origin fact is destination-neutral: issuance mechanism names no recipient board; attestation chain runs only to the origin's foreign ministry (Hague status stated) without naming a receiving mission; English-medium status is its own fact; search wording is origin-generic. The DESTINATION supplies the recipient, the final attestation step, its English rules, and its own search wording/FAQ.
_meta.why: v3's origin facts named the NMC as verification recipient (9/10) and the British High Commission as the final attestation step (8/9). That made them origin→UK facts, not origin facts — so Australia corridors could only name-swap, and the gate correctly cut all 10. This library disentangles them.
_meta.grounding: Same cited facts as v3, re-expressed neutrally — NO new claims. Sources carried from v3. Where a fact was inherently UK-specific (e.g. the NMC English routes), it is NOT an origin fact and lives on the destination block instead.
_meta.compose_instruction_for_CC: corridor(origin, destination) = originRegulator + goodStandingIssuance (append destination.verificationRecipient) + attestationBase (append destination attestation final-step per destinationParams) + englishMediumStatus (combine with destination English rules) + originSearchWording + destination.searchWording + destination FAQ. Shared destination process stays on /register/{dest} (law #3). Re-run the gate on Australia and REPORT by STATE — including same-origin cross-destination overlap (pakistan-UK vs pakistan-AU) so we can see honestly whether origin×destination is a real axis beyond the UK. Do not fill {origin_english_medium_status} by lifting cited clauses — it is now its own field below.
_meta.honest_expectation: This makes AU-only siblings distinct (real origin content differs across origins). The open question the gate must answer is same-origin cross-destination near-duplication. If those pairs still exceed the gate, the finding is that the value is per-destination pages + selective corridors, not a full N×M grid. Let the gate rule.

originRegulator.value: Pakistan Nursing & Midwifery Council (PNMC) — reconstituted/renamed from the former Pakistan Nursing Council (PNC).

goodStandingIssuance.value: PNMC issues verification of registration / good standing directly: the applicant submits the verification application form, a processing fee of PKR 10,000, a request letter from the receiving regulator/board (with full contact details), and photocopies of the PNMC registration card plus all nursing/midwifery diplomas and degrees. Queries go to PNMC's Good Standing Cell (gsc@pnmc.gov.pk). It is a manual/email-based process, not a self-service outbound portal.

attestationBase.value: Pakistani educational documents are attested via the Higher Education Commission (HEC) — with school/intermediate certificates countersigned by the IBCC — then by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Pakistan acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 9 March 2023), so MOFA now issues apostilles (apostille.mofa.gov.pk) after HEC/IBCC verification.

sources.name: HCCH — Pakistan accedes to Apostille Convention

englishMediumStatus.value: Pakistani pre-registration nursing's medium of instruction is variable, so an 'taught and examined in English' documentary route is often hard to evidence at the institution level.

originRegulator.value: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN). Main site nmcn.gov.ng; applicant portal myportal.nmcn.gov.ng; verification info nmcn.gov.ng/verify.html; payments via REMITA.

goodStandingIssuance.value: NMCN runs a 'Verification of Certificate' service: apply online on the Council's portal, upload a scanned Certificate(s) of Registration and a passport photo, complete the verification form naming the receiving regulator/board, and pay via REMITA. Only Certificate(s) of Registration are accepted (not exam-result/notification documents), and NMCN sends the verification directly to the receiving regulator. Revised guidelines (reported effective 1 March 2024) typically require ~2 years' post-qualification experience and an active practising licence; NMCN contacts the training institution and workplace directly; allow ~6 months. Fees (via REMITA) are reported around ₦66,875 standard, plus authentication ≈₦8,750 and a Letter of Good Standing ≈₦8,750.

attestationBase.value: Nigeria is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so Nigerian public documents are authenticated by the relevant Nigerian authorities and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (legalisation, not apostille). Confirm the exact chain for your document type.

englishMediumStatus.value: Nigerian pre-registration nursing is taught and examined in English, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).

originRegulator.value: The Indian Nursing Council (INC) sets national standards and runs the national live register (NRTS), but individual registration is held at the STATE Nursing Council level (under the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947).

goodStandingIssuance.value: India-distinct federal wrinkle: verification of registration / good standing for going abroad is issued by the STATE Nursing Council of first registration (e.g. Tamil Nadu TNMC, Kerala KNMC, Karnataka KSNC, Delhi DNC, Maharashtra MNC) — NOT the INC. The state council completes its section of the receiving regulator's verification form and sends it directly to that regulator; the applicant supplies passport, registration certificate, experience proof and the receiving authority's address. Some councils (e.g. Karnataka) include a video verification appointment. The INC runs national standards/register but does not issue foreign verification.

attestationBase.value: Indian public documents are authenticated at the State level (Home Department / HRD / SDM) and then apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). India is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so an MEA apostille is the final in-country step. State nursing-council verification is a separate credential step.

originRegulator.value: The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), through the Professional Regulatory Board of Nursing, issues the Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card (PIC) and provides certification/authentication and stateboard verification services. Online system: LERIS.

goodStandingIssuance.value: A Filipino nurse obtains PRC-authenticated documents via LERIS (log in, book an appointment, pay, present the Action Sheet plus valid PIC/e-PIC and originals with a Documentary Stamp Tax per copy), and the PRC provides a 'Stateboard Verification / Validation of Registration/License' service used by professionals going abroad. The PRC page does not describe direct electronic transmission to a specific overseas board; third-party verifiers (e.g. CGFNS/TruMerit, DataFlow) are commonly used depending on the destination — confirm the exact handoff for the receiving regulator.

attestationBase.value: The Philippines abolished the DFA 'red ribbon' and acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 14 May 2019; embassies stopped red ribbons 15 June 2019). Documents are now apostilled by the DFA (regular PHP 100, ~5 working days; expedited PHP 200, ~2 working days) at appointment.apostille.gov.ph.

englishMediumStatus.value: Philippine pre-registration nursing is taught and examined in English, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).

originRegulator.value: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana (NMC Ghana) registers and licenses Nurse Assistants, Nurses and Midwives in Ghana (nmc.gov.gh). Note the name collision with the UK NMC — different bodies.

goodStandingIssuance.value: NMC Ghana operates a Verification / Foreign Verification service (a good-standing / verification-of-registration route) for Ghana-registered practitioners applying to overseas boards; the practitioner's PIN must be current (annual renewal with CPD) before verification can be requested, and applications are handled through NMC Ghana regional offices with a 'Foreign Verification Steps' guide on the official site. Confirm the fee, timeline and transmission method with NMC Ghana (info@nmc.gov.gh).

attestationBase.value: Ghana is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so documents cannot be apostilled and require consular legalisation: Ghanaian public documents are authenticated by Ghana's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration (Accra) before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: English is Ghana's official language and the medium of nursing instruction, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).

originSearchWording: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana verification
Ghana Ministry of Foreign Affairs document authentication

originRegulator.value: The Nursing Council of Kenya (NCK), a statutory body under the Nurses Act (Cap 257). Public site nckenya.com; Online Services Portal osp.nckenya.com (government domain nckenya.go.ke).

goodStandingIssuance.value: NCK issues verification of registration / good standing to foreign regulators through an 'outmigration/emigration verification' service applied for via the NCK Online Services Portal (osp.nckenya.com); applicants submit national ID/passport, NCK professional certificate(s), a valid practising licence and the prescribed fee (destination-specific extras such as an employer reference, medical report, police clearance, CV and NEA proof may be required). The exact fee and timeline are not officially published — confirm with NCK.

sources.name: The Kenya Times — NCK emigration verification (secondary)

attestationBase.value: Kenya is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so Kenyan public documents require the full legalisation chain (not apostille): notarisation, authentication by the issuing body (e.g. NCK), then authentication by Kenya's Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs (MFDA) before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: English is an official language of Kenya and NCK examinations are in English, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).

originRegulator.value: The Nurses Council of Zimbabwe (NCZ), a statutory body under the Health Professions Act (Chapter 27:19). Official site nursescouncil.co.zw; registrant verification via nursesportal.nursescouncil.co.zw.

goodStandingIssuance.value: NCZ issues a Certificate of Good Standing (CGS) through its official 'Clearance form for Certificate of Good Standing Verification'. The applicant supplies personal and registration details, a 10-year employment history, criminal-record and disciplinary disclosures, intended destination and departure date, and two references from nurse managers in good standing; a Ministry of Health clearance is part of the process. The CGS is transmitted board-to-board — sent directly to the receiving Registrar — and NCZ may notify the receiving board of any matter arising after issue. The clearance process is stated to take about 1–2 weeks; an applicable fee is payable on submission (amount not published).

attestationBase.value: Zimbabwe is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so documents need full consular legalisation (not apostille): notarisation / High Court authentication, then authentication by the Zimbabwe Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Trade before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: Zimbabwean nurse education is delivered and examined in English, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).

originRegulator.value: Nursing in Egypt is regulated jointly by the Egyptian Nursing Syndicate (statutory body under Law 115 of 1976, maintaining the official register/membership card) and the Ministry of Health and Population (MoHP), which issues/renews the practising licence.

goodStandingIssuance.value: There is no single automated regulator-to-regulator verification for Egypt. The applicant obtains registration/good-standing evidence from the Egyptian Nursing Syndicate and the Ministry of Health and Population, then has it legalised through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (see attestation), and submits it to the receiving regulator, which assesses comparability.

attestationBase.value: Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so documents cannot be apostilled and must be legalised through the consular chain: Egyptian public documents are notarised/certified in Egypt then authenticated by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: Egyptian pre-registration nursing is generally taught in Arabic, so an English-medium documentary route is usually not available and an English test is normally required.

originRegulator.value: The Sri Lanka Nursing Council (SLNC) registers and regulates nurses in Sri Lanka, operating under the Ministry of Health portfolio (Sri Lanka Nurses Council Act). Official site slnc.lk.

goodStandingIssuance.value: The Sri Lanka-trained nurse obtains registration/good-standing proof from the SLNC as required by the receiving regulator, and applies to that regulator; documents are authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Affairs Division (see attestation). Confirm the exact good-standing document and process with the SLNC and the receiving regulator.

attestationBase.value: Sri Lanka is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so no apostille is issued; documents are authenticated/legalised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Affairs Division (Authentication & Verification Section) via its e-DAS system before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: Sri Lankan nursing medium of instruction varies (Sinhala/Tamil/English), so an English-medium documentary route is case-by-case and depends on the institution.

originRegulator.value: The Nepal Nursing Council (NNC), the statutory nursing regulator under the Nepal Nursing Council Act 2052 (1996), Bansbari, Kathmandu; it maintains the register and issues verification letters for nurses seeking recognition abroad. Official site nnc.org.np.

goodStandingIssuance.value: The NNC 'Verification' service requires an application letter to the Registrar, the receiving regulator's verification form (colour copy), both sides of a current NNC licence certificate, academic transcript, character certificate and passport ID page, plus the payment voucher; the official fee is NRs 2,500. The certificate is generally issued as a hard copy to the applicant rather than posted directly, so confirm the receiving regulator's direct-verification arrangement.

attestationBase.value: Nepal is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so documents need consular legalisation (not apostille): academic documents verified by the issuing university and/or Ministry of Education, then attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) consular department (app.nepalconsular.gov.np) before onward legalisation.

englishMediumStatus.value: Many Nepali pre-registration nursing programmes are delivered and examined in English, so an English-medium documentary route may be evidenced at the institution level (subject to the destination's rules).
